title: Nib's Perfect Pet
markdown:
Gadzooks! Nib the goblin had a super-duper important wish, more important than the sparkliest pebble or the yummiest berry. He wanted a pet.

He lived way up on the windy Sunspike Peaks, where the air whistled fun tunes through the rocky cliffs and clouds sometimes tickled his pointy ears. His home was cosy: piles of soft mossy cushions, glow-worm lanterns with a warm gentle light. It also felt a little bit lonely. He really, really wished for a furry, or maybe scaly, or even feathery friend to share his adventures.

“A pet!” he declared one blustery morning, bright green nose wiggling. The wind ruffled his spiky hair. “I need a pet!”

With a hop, skip, and a bounce he scurried down to the Whispering Woods, where friends were always happy to chat and share funny ideas. First he met Pipkin the Pixie, who zipped around his head like a speedy sparkly bumblebee. Rainbow wings left little trails of glitter.

“A pet, Nib? How absolutely thrilling!” Pipkin’s voice was tiny bells. “You should get a cloud-kitten! They float and purr like fluffy marshmallows, and they taste like sunshine on a warm day!”

Nib imagined a fluffy cloud purring on his lap, fur as soft as dandelion fluff. “But how do you catch a cloud-kitten, Pipkin? They seem so very high up!”

Pipkin winked. “That’s part of the fun! You’ll have to be quick and clever!”

Nib thanked her politely and did not leap at any clouds. Catching sunshine with your teeth, he decided, was a job for someone with longer arms.

Next he shuffled along a winding path, boots crunchy on fallen leaves, to find Bramble the Badger. Bramble was quietly sniffing a patch of nice-smelling thyme, whiskers wiggling. His voice was a low comforting rumble, like far-off thunder on a warm evening.

“A pet, you say? A very good idea.” A slow thoughtful nod. “I’d suggest a rock-biter. Very quiet. Super good at polishing stones. You’d always have the shiniest pebbles in the whole valley!”

Nib pictured a tiny creature with sharp teeth nibbling rocks. It sounded a bit dusty. He was not sure his cosy home would like all that rock dust. “What if it nibbled my favourite mossy cushion?”

Bramble stroked his chin whiskers. “A very good point. Perhaps a very small, very well-behaved burrow-owl? They keep the mice away.”

Nib’s head was spinning faster than Pipkin’s wings. Cloud-kittens that tasted like sunshine. Rock-biters that polished stones. Just then a huge shadow fell over the trees. Ignis the Dragon, emerald scales glinting like a thousand jewels in dappled sunlight, known everywhere for his loud voice and even louder, often bonkers, ideas.

“Ho there, little goblin!” The boom rattled the leaves like maracas. “Heard you’re looking for a friend! Step right up! A fire-lizard! They breathe little puffs of smoke—perfect for warming your toes on chilly nights!”

Nib imagined a tiny lizard puffing smoke into his cosy home. “What if it sets my glow-worm lanterns on fire, Mr. Ignis?” He loved those lanterns.

Ignis let out a great puff that smelled of burnt toast and adventure. “Nonsense! A tiny spark, that’s all! Perfectly safe! Or, if that’s not exciting enough, a grumpy griffin cub! Excellent at guarding things. No one would dare steal your berries!”

Nib gulped. A little lump in his throat. Tiny sharp claws. A very loud very grumpy squawk that would scare away all the friendly woodland creatures. His knees went wobbly, the way they did when a big choice sat on them. He was supposed to be choosing a friend. All the advice had become a tangled ball of yarn, knots and no end. He thanked everyone very politely, voice a little shaky, and wandered off, sad and very, very unsure.

He found himself on a high windswept ledge looking out over the big green valley. The wind tugged at his ears and spiky hair. He sat down with a big sigh, knees to chest. His bright green nose drooped. He felt like a lost mushroom, all alone and a bit soggy. Not brave enough for cloud-kittens. Too worried about rock-biter dust. Definitely not ready for grumpy griffins.

A tiny soft sound caught his ear. Delicate. Fluttering. Like leaves dancing. He peeked over the edge. On a little rocky spot, tucked among grey stones, was something very small and very fluffy. Ears like delicate green leaves, perfectly shaped. Eyes like two shiny black pebbles, bright and watching. It shivered a little in the strong wind, looking a bit lost and a bit lonely.

Nib’s heart did a happy hopeful flip. Not a cloud-kitten. Not a rock-biter. Not a fiery lizard. Just small. Quiet. A bit scared, the way he felt sometimes when big choices arrived.

Very, very slowly, he held out a finger. His hand trembled just a little. The little creature tilted its leaf-like head. Pebble eyes watched. Then a hesitant step. Tiny paws made no sound on the rock. It sniffed his finger with a tiny wet nose, warm and surprisingly soft. Then a tiny happy squeak, so sweet it made him smile.

A big wide toothy goblin smile, all the way to his pointy ears. This little creature did not need loud advice from dragons, or silly ideas from pixies, or even sensible suggestions from badgers. It just needed a friend. He scooped it into his hands. It snuggled into his palms at once, leaf-ears twitching happily.

He decided to call it Flicker, because its gentle spirit seemed to flicker with a soft warm light. As he carried Flicker home, the wind did not seem so lonely. The rocky cliffs did not seem so scary. Cloud-kittens and griffin cubs could keep their grandness. He had found his own special pet, and it fitted his pockets.

Back in the cosy home, Flicker explored the mossy cushions with curious little hops. Leaf-ears perked. Nib watched, heart warm and full like a freshly baked berry pie. The glow-worm lanterns stayed un-toasted. The favourite cushion stayed un-nibbled. Flicker chirped, a small brave sound, and Nib, who had not caught a single cloud, winked at the lanterns as if to say: seven pieces of advice with one quiet look. And that, for a goblin on a windy peak, was quite enough triumph for one morning.
characters: Nib (young goblin of Sunspike Peaks), Flicker (leaf-eared creature of the windy ledge)
